newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-Australian interest rates poll - May.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Australian interest rates poll - May.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) board met on Tuesday. Ahead of the meeting, Reuters asked 27 economists the following questions
1) Are you expecting a change in official interest rates to follow the May board meeting?
2) What direction do you expect the next move in interest rates will most likely be?
3) When will the next rate move take place?

There had been some analysts expecting a possible RBA move after the May board meeting, but the wages data on Thursday showing a quarterly rise of 1.3 percent and a 4.6 percent annual rate, has meant that such a move is now highly improbable, even if there are some doubts over the data.
While the results show that the next most likely move is expected to be a rise in early 1998, economists said the risks over the next three months or so were for a further cut.

What made them see a rise as more likely was that the pace of wages growth and signs of strength in leading indicators such as retail trading and the housing sector would give the RBA breathing space to hold rates steady while it waited for the economy to improve.

However, the ongoing weakness of the labour market remained a real concern, and another few months of weakness, expecially if other indicators also showed softness, may be enough to bring about a rate cut.

Inflation, despite Thursday's higher than expected wages data, was not seen as an obstacle to a rate cut. If however, wages, and enterprise bargaining agreements, showed signs of increasing then rate cut prospects would be damaged.
The longer a cut was held off by the RBA, the more likely it was that it the next move in rates would be a rise.
But reflecting the fact that a cut was still seen as a real possibility, most economists saw any rate hike as being at least nine months.
JP Morgan No Unchanged forseeable future
